smell: README Usage+Phase sections document commands and flags that do not exist in code: 'okdctl version' subcommand (only --version flag is wired), '--skip-terraform', '--skip-isos', '--skip-haproxy', '--skip-dns' (no such flags on deploy). Uninstall section (line 175-177) also claims '--remove-packages' toggles package removal; in practice destroy hardcodes removePackages=true (internal/cli/destroy.go:78).
evidence:
okdctl version          print version, git commit, build date
...
Bring your own infra with --skip-terraform (existing VMs), --skip-isos
(your own ignition), --skip-haproxy, or --skip-dns.
...
'--remove-packages' also uninstalls haproxy, dnsmasq, httpd
severity_reason: User runs the command from README and hits 'unknown command/flag' error; doc-side half of a documented cli-ux seam; first impression for every new contributor.
fix_summary: Rewrite README Usage and 'A deploy runs three phases' sections to match the actual command surface: drop the 'okdctl version' row (replace with 'okdctl --version'), drop the --skip-* sentence (those flags do not exist), and remove the '--remove-packages' paragraph in Uninstall. If the flags are intended future work, flag them explicitly under a 'Planned' header — not under Usage.
must_preserve: README tone/sections that match shipped UX; only rewrite the drift lines.

smell: docs/architecture/phases.md shows BasePhase with Exec, Log, Version, OS, and Pkg fields. The actual struct (internal/distribution/okd/phase/paths.go:50-54) has only Exec, Log, Version — OS (platform.OS) and Pkg (packages.Manager) are absent. The doc misrepresents the canonical phase substrate a new contributor would grep for.
evidence:
type BasePhase struct {
    Exec    *executor.Executor  // subprocess runner (oc, terraform, etc.)
    Log     *slog.Logger        // structured logger
    Version string              // OKD version string, for display
    OS      platform.OS         // OS family detection
    Pkg     packages.Manager    // dnf/apt wrapper
}
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — BasePhase is a CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes canonical API; doc drift on the canonical type misleads every downstream author.
fix_summary: Update phases.md snippet to match internal/distribution/okd/phase/paths.go — drop the OS and Pkg fields. If the OS/Pkg fields are planned, move them into a 'Planned' sub-section and link the roadmap entry.
must_preserve: The rest of phases.md's prose accurately describes the orchestrator flow.

smell: docs/architecture/addons.md shows an Addon interface that does not match code: Info() returns 'Info' but code returns AddonInfo; ValidateSettings(map[string]any) error is declared on Addon, but code places ValidateSettings(map[string]string) []string on a separate ConfigurableAddon interface. New addon authors following the doc will write signatures that don't compile.
evidence:
type Addon interface {
    Info() Info                                      // name, display name, deps, etc.
    ValidateSettings(settings map[string]any) error  // check user inputs
    Install(ctx context.Context, env *Environment) error
    Verify(ctx context.Context, env *Environment) error
    Uninstall(ctx context.Context, env *Environment) error
}
severity_reason: Contract-level doc that instructs contributors to write non-compiling code; every new addon is a blocking friction point.
fix_summary: Rewrite the interface snippet to match internal/addon/addon.go:13-19 (AddonInfo return type, 4 methods) and introduce a second block for ConfigurableAddon showing DefaultSettings + the actual ValidateSettings signature. Add a pointer: 'settings maps are flat string→string; use ConfigurableAddon if you need wizard inputs.'
must_preserve: Nothing — this is a correctness fix.

smell: Package cli has two separate '// Package cli ...' doc blocks (root.go:1-4 and confirm.go:1-3) with overlapping but non-identical summaries. Go concatenates both into godoc, producing two paragraphs that re-introduce the package twice. CLAUDE.md §code-comments item 1 calls for one block of 1-3 sentences; splitting it across files violates that shape.
fix_summary: Keep the root.go block (it carries the exit-code contract callers care about); demote confirm.go's leading comment to a regular non-package doc comment that describes promptForConfirmation, not the package. Alternative: merge both summaries into root.go and strip confirm.go's // Package cli header.
must_preserve: The exit-code contract (codes 2/3/4/5/1/130/0) in root.go must survive in whichever block is kept.

smell: Package platform has two '// Package platform ...' doc blocks (platform.go:1-5 and packages.go:1-7). godoc shows both — the first block explicitly says 'see platform.go for the package summary' which is a godoc anti-pattern (the reader is already reading godoc, not the source). Package doc should live in one file.
evidence: // Package platform — see platform.go for the package summary. This file\n// implements the OS-agnostic PackageManager abstraction, with a single\n// Manager type driven by per-family binary names (dnf/apt-get, rpm/dpkg)
fix_summary: Strip the '// Package platform' prefix from packages.go and leave the existing file-scoped commentary as a plain block comment (or delete it — the body is self-explanatory). platform.go keeps the sole package-level block.
rule_source: Effective Go §Commentary — package comment 'appears in the first file of the package that has a comment'
must_preserve: The factual content about Manager's stderr-capture design — move it to a comment on the Manager type itself if it needs a home.

smell: Exported Summary struct and GenerateSummary function have no doc comments. Summary carries counts/sizes whose semantics (what counts as 'remaining'?) aren't evident from field names; GenerateSummary touches the filesystem (Stat, Glob, ReadDir) — caller contract about side-effects belongs in a doc comment.
fix_summary: Add a 2-sentence doc to Summary ('snapshot of residual cleanup artefacts …') and a 1-2 sentence doc to GenerateSummary describing what 'Remaining*' means post-Execute and that it does filesystem I/O. If api-design settles that GenerateSummary should be unexported (see related), delete instead of documenting.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §code-comments item 2 (exported API with non-obvious behavior)
must_preserve: Nothing — pure doc add or delete.

smell: The step/orchestrator contract interfaces and builder methods lack doc comments: StepID, StepResult, Step, Skipper, FatalChecker, StepCallbacks, ProvisioningStep, StepBuilder, and the nine Description/Fatal/SkipWhen/SkipReason/OnStart/OnComplete/OnError/Execute/Build methods. Builder methods can share one group doc if the fluent chain is self-describing ('each returns *StepBuilder for chaining'). StepID can stay undocumented (string alias, name explains it).
must_preserve: Existing NewStepBuilder, MustBuild, StepDef, BuildSteps docs.

smell: Orchestrator, NewOrchestrator, SetLogger, and Run have no doc comments; only Results carries a concurrency note. Run's semantics (stops on first fatal error, skipped steps logged) and SetLogger's nil-guard are caller-visible contracts that should live on the symbols.
fix_summary: Add: 'Orchestrator executes ProvisioningSteps sequentially and aggregates StepResult …', 'NewOrchestrator …', 'SetLogger … nil loggers are ignored', 'Run executes steps until ctx cancels or a fatal step fails …'.

smell: ServiceAction string-enum, the seven Service* constants, ManageService, IsServiceActive, IsServiceEnabled lack doc. Each has non-obvious Linux-only behavior: ManageService errors on non-Linux, but the 'Is*' helpers return false (not error). fix_summary: Add: 'ServiceAction is the systemctl verb …' group doc on the constants; 'ManageService invokes systemctl <action> <service>; returns error on non-Linux'; 'IsServiceActive … returns false on non-Linux (not an error, by design — callers poll in tight loops)'. Mirror the same note on IsServiceEnabled.
